name: South Korea
headline: Bold, fiery, and unapologetically slurpable.
intro: Korea eats more instant noodles per person than almost anywhere on earth, and it shows. Expect deep red gochugaru broths, smoky black-bean jjajang, cheesy fire-noodle mash-ups and the cult-favourite Buldak range that dares you to go one level hotter.

name: Japan
headline: Where instant noodles were born.
intro: Momofuku Ando invented instant ramen in Osaka in 1958, and Japan has been perfecting it ever since. Think silky tonkotsu, nutty sesame oil, rich Hokkaido miso, glossy Tokyo shoyu and saucy yakisoba — clean, balanced and deeply savoury.

name: Indonesia
headline: Home of the world's favourite mi goreng.
intro: Indonesia is one of the biggest instant noodle markets on the planet, and Mi Goreng is its gift to the world: sweet soy, fried shallots and chilli tossed through springy noodles. Add soto, baso and curry soups and you have a whole archipelago in a bowl.

name: Vietnam
headline: Bright, zesty, herb-fresh bowls.
intro: Vietnam's instant noodles lean light and aromatic — hot-and-sour shrimp, golden chicken, pho-style beef and Thai-inspired lau hotpot flavours. Fast, fragrant and incredibly easy to love.

name: China
headline: The biggest noodle nation of them all.
intro: China eats more instant noodles than any other country. Braised beef is the national classic, but there is so much more: numbing mala, Chongqing chilli, pickled mustard greens, hot-and-sour and slow-braised rib broths.

name: Malaysia
headline: Hawker-stall flavours, instantly.
intro: Malaysia brings Penang's legendary street food to the packet: creamy white curry, tangy asam laksa, sweet-savoury Hokkien prawn and rich fish broths. Some of the most awarded instant noodles in the world come from here.

name: Thailand
headline: Sour, spicy, salty, sweet — all at once.
intro: Thailand's tom yum is the icon here: lemongrass, lime and chilli in a punchy, aromatic broth. Mama and Wai Wai are household names, joined by rich pork, seafood and even a Michelin-inspired collab.

name: Singapore
headline: Small island, huge flavour.
intro: Singapore punches way above its weight with premium, restaurant-style noodles — buttery salted egg, rich laksa and fiery mala. Indulgent, a little bit fancy and seriously addictive.

name: India
headline: Masala magic in two minutes.
intro: In India, a bowl of masala noodles is pure nostalgia — warming spices, a little tang and a lot of comfort. Most of these cook down to a saucy, spice-coated finish that's made for slurping.

name: Philippines
headline: Pancit Canton: the family favourite.
intro: Lucky Me! Pancit Canton is a staple in Filipino homes — stir-fried style noodles with sweet, savoury and citrusy kalamansi notes. Simple, saucy and impossible to stop at one.

name: Taiwan
headline: Night-market noodles with real chew.
intro: Taiwan's sun-dried, hand-pulled style noodles have a bouncy, restaurant-quality bite. Dress them in danzai sauce, scallion oil, braised beef or nutty dan dan for a proper night-market feel.

name: Australia
headline: The lunchbox legend.
intro: Every Aussie knows the 2 Minute Noodle. Maggi's chicken, beef and oriental flavours are the comfort-food classics so many of us grew up on — and they still hit the spot.
